translations.translation: "As an eagle stirs up its nest, [hovers over its young, spreads its wings, takes them, carries them on its pinions]"
And the explanation of the Baal HaHilula (the master of the yahrzeit) is known,
that an eagle is the aspect of mercy,
and "as an eagle stirs up" is the aspect of abundant mercy.
And what is written "carries them on its pinions,"
even though He has no body and no bodily form,
this is because "this is the Torah, man,"
and this is the matter of the 248 limbs of the King, which are made through the 248 positive commandments,
that through the fulfillment of the commandments, [the Holy One, blessed be He, says] "I consider it as if you have made Me."
And this is the matter of "carries them on its pinions,"
that from the aspect of the abundant mercy of the level of "eagle," behold, through teshuvah there is an elevation above the aspect of the 248 limbs of the King that come through the commandments
("carries them on its pinions").
And this corresponds with what is explained in Kabbalah,
that the living creatures of the Chariot are illuminated by the thirteen rectifications of the Beard,
and higher still, "eagle" is the aspect of Atik, which is removed and separated from the entire order of Hishtalshelus (the chain of descent),
therefore, from the aspect of this level, there are no measurements or limitations,
not even the measurements of the highest levels within the order of Hishtalshelus,
and even the measurements of Torah and commandments.
And therefore, from the aspect of this level, "carries them on its pinions."
And it can be said, in a manner of a possible explanation, that this is also the reason why we read Parshas Haazinu during the Ten Days of Repentance or immediately after Yom Kippur,
because then is the time of teshuvah,
when even one who sinned,
whether a sin in its simple sense or a sin from the term "deficiency," as it is written,
"I and my son Shlomo are sinners,"
meaning that he is lacking in the perfection of his service,
behold, from the revelation of the aspect of "eagle,"
through teshuvah there is an elevation above the aspect of "its pinions."
